overview.summary: Bosch uses a systematic approach to measurement and spacing in digital design based on the rem (root EM) unit. The system supports consistency, accessibility, proportional scaling, responsive design, and alignment between design and development across devices, screen resolutions, and touchpoints.
overview.core_rule: Use root EM (rem) as the basic unit of measurement for digital components.

standard_base.label: 1 rem = 16 px
standard_base.scope: Websites, software, mobile apps, and other standard digital touchpoints
standard_base.exception: Product user interfaces may vary depending on use case, hardware, physical pixel density, and spatial conditions.

applies_to: Product user interfaces where adapted to hardware and use case
scope.design_problem: Bosch develops applications for many devices, screen resolutions, and use cases, so component sizes may differ across applications. A common rem-based measurement model keeps specifications clear and broadly applicable.

principles.name: Visibility and readability
principles.description: Dimensions and sizes must be easy to perceive in the intended use situation.

principles.name: Consistency & predictability
principles.description: Uniform sizes must be used consistently for similar elements to meet user expectations and make orientation easier.
considerations: Similar elements should use similar sizing
Patterns should remain predictable across interfaces

principles.name: Context of use and accessibility
principles.description: Stationary and portable mobile systems must both be considered so that appropriate sizes are selected for each application.

rem_grid.definition: The rem unit (root EM) is based on the font size of the HTML root element, usually <html>. 1 rem corresponds to the base font size.
benefits: Creates proportional scaling across screen resolutions
Allows display enlargement or reduction through browser settings
Strengthens coherence between design and development
rem_grid.design_development_alignment: 1 rem acts as a universal reference point for spacing, sizes, and typography, enabling systematic design across platforms and devices.

defaults.description: Bosch uses modular rem-based default values for spacing and sizing. The documented scale ends at 16 rem but can be extended when needed.
defaults.implementation_note: Use the scale consistently to keep layouts visually balanced and functional across device types.

scaling.description: Different digital products may use different measurement or positioning units, but Bosch's 1-rem system provides the shared reference point.

standard_touchpoints.name: Websites
standard_touchpoints.relationship_to_system: Uses the standard 1 rem = 16 px reference.

standard_touchpoints.name: Mobile Apps
standard_touchpoints.relationship_to_system: Uses the standard 1 rem = 16 px reference.

standard_touchpoints.name: Software
standard_touchpoints.relationship_to_system: Uses the standard 1 rem = 16 px reference.

standard_touchpoints.name: Digital Newsletter
standard_touchpoints.relationship_to_system: Uses the standard 1 rem = 16 px reference.

standard_touchpoints.name: Banner
standard_touchpoints.relationship_to_system: Uses the standard 1 rem = 16 px reference.

product_ui_hardware.description: For product user interfaces, size representation depends on spatial conditions, use case, hardware, and physical pixel density. Requirements for readability in mobility contexts may be based on ISO and DIN standards.
product_ui_hardware.reference_standard_mentioned: ISO 9241-161 - Ergonomics of human-system interaction - Part 161: Guidelines for visual user interface elements

do.rule: Consider measurement and spacing in context.
do.details: Account for touchpoints, devices, intended use, viewing distance, input methods, ambient light, and interaction frequency.
Apply rem-based grids to support consistency, ergonomics, and accessibility.
Use spacing to express relationships and hierarchy between elements.

dont.details: Avoid extreme distances that break logical grouping or weaken perceived relationships.

dont.rule: Do not design without accessibility context.
dont.details: Avoid dimensions and spacing that make interaction challenging or create a negative user experience.

areas.title: Setup & structure
areas.purpose: Establish a clear layout foundation before applying detailed spacing decisions.

areas.title: Design grid
areas.purpose: Use a consistent grid to structure dimensions, spacing, and alignment.

areas.title: Design with Figma
areas.purpose: Apply measurement and spacing rules systematically in design tooling.

areas.title: Accessibility
areas.purpose: Ensure measurements, spacing, and scale support accessible perception and interaction.

when_generating_ui: Use rem as the primary spacing and sizing reference unless a product UI hardware context requires adaptation.
Default to 1 rem = 16 px for standard digital touchpoints.
Use the documented modular spacing scale before inventing intermediate values.
Adjust sizing decisions based on viewing distance, ambient light, input method, and accessibility needs.
when_reviewing_ui: Check if similar elements use uniform sizes and spacing.
Check whether spacing supports logical grouping and hierarchy.
Check if dimensions remain readable and usable in the intended context.
Check whether rem-based values can scale proportionally.
